note: Hand-written. These are readings of individual candidates by a person, and
they are kept in their own file, marked as judgement, because a judgement
that looks like a measurement is what cost the sibling project a published
restatement -- the stronger form is a sibling the library states, or one a
narrow      -- a different theorem: the proof was about something else
artefact    -- the tool is wrong about this row
witness     -- the proof names an object the statement quantifies away;
stage 2's material rather than a stronger proposition
A row absent from this file was NOT read. Unread is not the same as clean.

Real.log_surjective: the witness is `exp` and the stronger statement IS `Real.log_exp`, which the library states one file away. Caught by the duplicate check, which is the outcome that validates it
Real.monotoneOn_sin: `Real.strictMonoOn_sin` exists. This is BRIEF.md's own failing condition -- the sharper sibling on the next line -- and it was caught rather than reported
continuousAt_id: `continuous_id` is one of the most cited lemmas in Mathlib; a reader grants this on sight
uniformEquicontinuous_empty: true but vacuous: the index type is empty, so the unfolded form carries nothing the statement did not
Cardinal.mk_le_of_injective: the statement is a cardinal inequality; the proof constructs an explicit embedding `α ↪ β`. The embedding is the content and the statement discards it
Finset.HasAntidiagonal.nonempty_antidiag: states that the antidiagonal is nonempty, proves that `(0, a)` is in it. Naming the element is strictly more useful than asserting one exists
Height.mulHeight₁_nonneg: `0 ≤ h x` stated, `0 < h x` proved. Strict positivity of a height is a different fact from non-negativity
Polynomial.ne_natDegree_of_mem_eraseLead: `a ≠ natDegree f` stated, `a < natDegree f` proved. The order relation is real information the disequality drops
Multiset.powerset_mono: Monotone stated, StrictMono proved, and no `strictMono` sibling was found in the module
continuous_descPochhammer_eval: continuity stated, differentiability proved. A different theorem about the same function
Isometry.mapsTo_eball: `MapsTo` stated, an equality of preimages proved
Filter.tendsto_swap4_prod: `Tendsto` stated, an equality of pushforward filters proved
Finset.EquitableOn.le: a one-sided bound stated, the two-sided bound proved
sum_col_of_mem_doublyStochastic: column sums stated, rows AND columns proved
Ordnode.Valid.merge: validity stated, validity together with the size identity proved
Nat.sInf_empty: states `sInf ∅ = 0`, offers `∅ = ∅`. Wrapper stripping cut the chain; the statement is true and unrelated. Now caught as `unchained`
EuclideanGeometry.dist_orthogonalProject: states an equality of distances, offers one of angles. Same cause, five layers of wrappers
ne_of_ssuperset: states `b ⊂ a → a ≠ b` and offers `b ⊂ a → b ⊂ a`. The selected argument is the hypothesis itself, so the stronger statement restates an assumption
RatFunc.denom_inv_dvd: divisibility stated, the exact formula for the inverse proved. Genuinely wanted, and `unchained`: true and verified, but the chain to the stated theorem is not established by the table
Cardinal.natCast_lt_aleph0: `↑n < ℵ₀` stated, `Fin (n+1) ↪ ℕ` proved. Also `unchained`, and also real
Module.Relations.Solution.IsPresentation: surjectivity of one map stated, bijectivity of a related map proved. `unchained`
NormedAlgebra.Complex.nonempty_algEquiv: Gelfand-Mazur: `Nonempty (ℂ ≃ₐ[ℂ] F)` stated, the equivalence itself constructed. The canonical isomorphism is an object nobody named here
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.OneH: a hypercover is constructed and then forgotten
FirstOrder.Language.Theory.simpleGraph_i: satisfiability stated, an actual model produced
CategoryTheory.SmallCategoryCardinalLT.e: an explicit small category is built and existentially hidden
isBoundedUnder_le_finset_sup': boundedness stated, an explicit eventual bound proved
CategoryTheory.section_comp_right: one composition identity stated, both proved -- though the witness goes through `Classical.choose`, which stage 2 will classify as noncomputable
LinearOrderedAddCommGroup.Subgroup.negGe: negativity of the generator stated, negativity together with the generation property proved; also via `Classical.choose`
